steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Whisk 1 cup flour and salt together in a bowl; mix in ½ cup room temperature butter until it resembles cornmeal. Stir in 3 tablespoons ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until dough holds together. Refrigerate dough until ready to use.
Place blackberries in a large bowl; sprinkle with sugar and 6 tablespoons flour. Stir in ¾ cup water until moistened; transfer filling to a 2-quart baking dish.

Roll out dough on a floured work surface to ¼-inch thickness; cut into ¾-inch strips. Place 2 dough strips, starting with the longest strips, in an X in the center of filling. Alternate horizontal and vertical strips, weaving them in an over-and-under pattern. Use the shortest strips for the edges of the lattice. Scatter ½ cup cold diced butter over top.
Bake in the preheated oven until berries are tender and crust is golden brown, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Brandy's Blackberry Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: Brandy's blackberry cobbler recipe makes a lovely hot fruit-forward cobbler with a flaky, buttery crisscross lattice crust that decorates the top.

review.reviewBody: Delicious recipe! Simple to make, and a real crowd pleaser!

Put the pie crust on the bottom & add a delicious gooey top that covers it all! This recipe has a superb berry mixture but I cooked my homegrown blackberries on med low with the sugar, 1/2 the water, tsp of vanilla, dash of lemon juice, dash of cinnamon, & dash of nutmeg first. Added the flour & rest of water for last few min & it thickened up perfect. After reading reviews about how this version didn't have enough topping, I read a peach cobbler recipe here, & a man adjusted one to include his grandmother's top-and it's what I have been searching for, the traditional gooey type. I put this recipe's rolled crust on the bottom of a large Pyrex casserole bowl, next scooped (spatula needed) the berry mixture onto the crust, then layered 1 1/2 cups of each on top: flour, sugar & milk-Sprinkling some of each alternately, then dotted it with butter all over (about 4-6 tablespoons). Baked uncovered at 400 for 40 min. & then lowered temp to 350 for another 20 min or until it started to brown & turn solid on top. Fantastic texture & best ever!

Very good! Here’s what I changed and would change in the future. I added 1/2 sugar, 1/2 brown sugar, but I think in the future I’d add about a 1/4 c less sugar, as it is sweet. Also, I’d make more crust, I love a lot of crust, so would maybe do 1.5 times the crust recipe. I omitted the water to the blackberry mix, as I figured they’d be plenty juicy and wouldn’t require more liquid, and for me, it worked out great..nice and thick! I added 1/2 tsp vanilla and a heaping tsp of cinnamon to the blackberry mixture, yum!

I recommend to put a pie crust on bottom as well, cut the water to 1/2 cup, and put 1/4 cup more sugar into Berry mixture. Looks great but a little too tart, extremely runny, and very little bread. With a few modifications it would be perfect.

Good recipe. I made a couple of minor changes. The dough was a bit too stiff and dry, especially after refrigerating so I added another 3 TBS of ice water. I used less water (only 1/4 cup in the blackberries and added about a TBS of lemon juice and a tsp of vanilla. I also used slightly less sugar (about 1 cup) just because I don't like it really sweet.

This is the best cobbler ever and I thought my peach cobbler topped all! I added a teaspoon of lemon juice, 1/2 teaspoon vanilla and 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg. So good!! Oh I had a package of frozen raspberries that I thawed and added since I like lots of berries. I did reduce the water to 1/2 cup and the cobbler was wonderful.

This is such a good cobbler! I have made it twice. My family loved it. I cut the sugar in half bc we don’t eat much sugar. The crust is dreamy. It’s important to refrigerate the dough as the recipe specifies as I didn’t the 2nd time and it wasn’t as good.

This was easy and turned out great. My grandkids and I enjoyed it. I should have noted reviews as I added the full 3/4 cup water to berry mixture. I immediately recognized it was too much and siphoned out 1/4 cup of syrup - glad i did or it would have been too soupy. I toyed with adding extra sugar to replace what I took out but glad I didn’t as it was great heated with a bit of ice cream. I saved the syrup - good over plain ice cream!

It took 1 hour for the filling to completely cook with the oven preheated at 400*. I used ready made crust in a glass 9” round pie pan. I added foil to the edges to prevent over browning. It tastes amazing with out the tartness.
Excellent recipe! I only added a teaspoon of lemon juice to the berries and cut the sugar amount a little for health reasons. It turned out delicious!

Delicious!! All I could find were cobbler recipes that were more like cake, which makes it less fruity - This was exactly what I was looking for. I used store-bought crust, so this was quite easy. I halved the sugar and butter, and it was still out of this world!!
So yummy. I actually used a refrigerated pie crust to save time. Still great!
This was the easiest and most flavorful cobbler I've ever made!
Best blackberry cobbler I've ever made. My family loved it and paused when I told them I made it. They couldn't believe it. lol. Thanks for sharing.
Ridiculously good and easy to make. Cheers!
My husband loves this recipe. I use about half the sugar then top it with vanilla ice cream. Wonderful!
Made this cobbler with wild blackberries from our pasture. It was a big hit and I will save this recipe!!
